# Kernel Managed Auth migration

Website sign-in now uses one generic Kernel Managed Auth integration. Kernel
owns login discovery, REDACTED entry, account choices and interactive SMS/email
verification. There are no merchant-specific selectors, phone rewrites or retry
rules in this migration.

Clanker privately delivers an authenticated owner-only link and carries the
original task context internally. A pending flow is reused; starting another
login would cancel the old Kernel flow. The original task resumes only after the
same owned flow reports `SUCCESS` and its connection reports `AUTHENTICATED`.
Failed or expired flows need a fresh ordinary owner request, without an exact
approval phrase or automatic SMS loop.

Each workspace/requester/account/task has an isolated profile. Automation opens
a fresh browser with the successful snapshot and explicit `save_changes: false`.
Owner membership, invitations, request state and remote profile identity are
checked before attachment. Cancellation, revocation and delayed cleanup cannot
revive a request or delete a replacement flow. Unconfirmed dispatch and cleanup
remain blocked for reconciliation.

Existing Vault login items stay protected. Kernel documents no import bridge
from their write-only fields into Managed Auth credentials, so first sign-in may
require credentials again. Personal details and approved backend API-key
execution continue through Kernel Vault.

## Verification

- Canonical runner: 22 scoped files, **769 passed, 0 failed**, frozen source
  unchanged. The first run caught a compatibility schema regression; the final
  run preserves the declarative, value-free legacy alias schema.
- Real disposable Kernel checks verified hosted login creation, HTTP 200 for
  the hosted page, exact proxy/profile identity, read-only profile attachment,
  terminal flow handling, and verified browser/connection/profile deletion.
- Real responses use `managed-auth.onkernel.com`, normalize expiry formatting,
  and omit the hosted URL after a terminal flow. Regression checks cover each.
- Synthetic probes used no real account credentials, SMS requests, Slack
  messages or purchases. Actual Gmail and merchant/SMS authentication require
  user participation and are not established by these probes.

Protected proof: `.local/kernel-only-20261008/managed-auth-tests-final-v2-20261009.json`.

## Activation

Activated after the previous gateway was healthy and idle. The reviewed drain
completed, old PID 57398 exited, and one replacement launch became healthy as
PID 66853. Slack's writer identity, fresh heartbeat and session store passed.
Frozen source and protected configuration stayed unchanged.

Post-activation checks confirmed Managed Auth initialized in the live database,
the authentication tool registered, local and public web health returned HTTP
200, and unauthenticated or foreign-origin requests were rejected. These checks
do not establish a real account login.

Two expired orphaned OTP collection items from the old implementation were
deleted with remote absence checks. Only their exact local request statuses
changed to cancelled. The saved Gmail login, other credentials and task context
were preserved.

`.local/kernel-only-20261008/managed-auth-activation-20261009.json` and
`.local/kernel-only-20261008/managed-auth-post-activation-20261009.json`.

[Hosted UI](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/auth/hosted-ui),
[SMS/email limitations](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/auth/faq), and
[profile concurrency](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/browsers/profiles/concurrency).

# Kernel Managed Auth migration

Website sign-in now uses one generic Kernel Managed Auth integration. Kernel
owns login discovery, REDACTED entry, account choices and interactive SMS/email
verification. There are no merchant-specific selectors, phone rewrites or retry
rules in this migration.

Clanker privately delivers an authenticated owner-only link and carries the
original task context internally. A pending flow is reused; starting another
login would cancel the old Kernel flow. The original task resumes only after the
same owned flow reports `SUCCESS` and its connection reports `AUTHENTICATED`.
Failed or expired flows need a fresh ordinary owner request, without an exact
approval phrase or automatic SMS loop.

Each workspace/requester/account/task has an isolated profile. Automation opens
a fresh browser with the successful snapshot and explicit `save_changes: false`.
Owner membership, invitations, request state and remote profile identity are
checked before attachment. Cancellation, revocation and delayed cleanup cannot
revive a request or delete a replacement flow. Unconfirmed dispatch and cleanup
remain blocked for reconciliation.

Existing Vault login items stay protected. Kernel documents no import bridge
from their write-only fields into Managed Auth credentials, so first sign-in may
require credentials again. Personal details and approved backend API-key
execution continue through Kernel Vault.

## Verification

- Canonical runner: 22 scoped files, **769 passed, 0 failed**, frozen source
  unchanged. The first run caught a compatibility schema regression; the final
  run preserves the declarative, value-free legacy alias schema.
- Real disposable Kernel checks verified hosted login creation, HTTP 200 for
  the hosted page, exact proxy/profile identity, read-only profile attachment,
  terminal flow handling, and verified browser/connection/profile deletion.
- Real responses use `managed-auth.onkernel.com`, normalize expiry formatting,
  and omit the hosted URL after a terminal flow. Regression checks cover each.
- Synthetic probes used no real account credentials, SMS requests, Slack
  messages or purchases. Actual Gmail and merchant/SMS authentication require
  user participation and are not established by these probes.

Protected proof: `.local/kernel-only-20261008/managed-auth-tests-final-v2-20261009.json`.

## Activation

Activated after the previous gateway was healthy and idle. The reviewed drain
completed, old PID 57398 exited, and one replacement launch became healthy as
PID 66853. Slack's writer identity, fresh heartbeat and session store passed.
Frozen source and protected configuration stayed unchanged.

Post-activation checks confirmed Managed Auth initialized in the live database,
the authentication tool registered, local and public web health returned HTTP
200, and unauthenticated or foreign-origin requests were rejected. These checks
do not establish a real account login.

Two expired orphaned OTP collection items from the old implementation were
deleted with remote absence checks. Only their exact local request statuses
changed to cancelled. The saved Gmail login, other credentials and task context
were preserved.

Protected activation and post-check receipts:
`.local/kernel-only-20261008/managed-auth-activation-20261009.json` and

Confirmed three local defects:

1. **Retries do not resend.** [service.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/service.py:332) immediately returns when `message_ts` exists. [managed_auth.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/managed_auth.py:310) still tells the model the link “was sent.” This directly explains repeated resend claims without new Slack messages.

2. **Delivery has no recovery location.** The link is posted into the saved source thread at [service.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/service.py:350), but no permalink or placement receipt reaches the model. The worker also ignores recorded deliveries because [store.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/store.py:220) retries only requests with null `message_ts`.

3. **Delivery deduplication misses concurrency and thread recovery.** Calls can race between history lookup and posting. Recovery checks channel history at [service.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/service.py:338), without explicitly reading the thread where it posts.

Recommended regressions:

1. Ordinary repeated authentication returns `already_sent`, preserves one auth flow, and supplies a requester-safe Slack permalink.
2. Explicit link resend creates one additional Slack message while preserving request, token, connection, and provider login count.
3. Replaying/concurrently processing the same owner event creates only one resend.
4. Recovery finds a previously posted threaded message after a database-write interruption.
5. Cancelled, expired, automatic-continuation, and invited-owner cases cannot trigger unauthorized resend or leak another owner’s private permalink.

The current [duplicate-login test](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/verification/probes/test_kernel_managed_auth.py:145) enforces one POST but does not check truthful delivery wording. No files or external state changed.

    async def deliver_link(self, row, *, delivery_event_id=None):
        # A resend is a new Slack delivery, never a new provider login or code.
        # The event comes from the authenticated turn, not a model argument.
        if delivery_event_id is not None and (not isinstance(delivery_event_id, str) or
                not re.fullmatch(r'[0-9]{10,}\.[0-9]{6}', delivery_event_id)):
            raise AccessError('Resending a private link requires a current Slack request.', 409)
        lock = self.link_delivery_locks.setdefault(row['id'], asyncio.Lock())
        async with lock:
            return await self._deliver_link(row['id'], delivery_event_id)

    async def _link_delivery_receipt(self, row, member, message_ts, status):
        source = json.loads(row['source'])
        receipt = {'status': status,
                   'recipient': 'account_owner' if row.get('approver') else 'requester',
                   'location': 'private_thread' if source.get('thread_id') and not row.get('approver') else 'private_dm'}
        # An invited account's owner receives the form in their own private DM.
        # Never return that DM's permalink to the requester.
        get_link = getattr(self.policy.client(), 'chat_getPermalink', None)
        if not row.get('approver') and get_link is not None:
            try:
                result = await get_link(channel=member['dm_id'], message_ts=message_ts)
                url = result.get('permalink')
                parts = urlsplit(url) if isinstance(url, str) else None
                if (parts and parts.scheme == 'https' and parts.hostname and
                        parts.hostname.endswith('.slack.com') and not parts.username and
                        not parts.password and not parts.query and not parts.fragment):
                    receipt['message_url'] = url
            except Exception:
                pass  # Delivery is committed even if its permalink is unavailable.
        return receipt

    async def _deliver_link(self, request_id, delivery_event_id):
        def current_request():
            with self.store.connection() as db:
                current = db.execute('SELECT * FROM requests WHERE id=?', (request_id,)).fetchone()
            if not current or current['status'] != 'waiting' or current['expires'] <= self.store.clock():
                raise AccessError('This private access request expired or was cancelled.', 410)
            return dict(current)

        row = current_request()
        member = self.validate_member(row['team'],row.get('approver') or row['owner'])
        if delivery_event_id == row.get('gateway_event_id'):
            delivery_event_id = None
        event_id = delivery_event_id or 'initial'
        with self.store.connection() as db:

    async def authenticate(self, turn, *, handle=None, origin=None, resend_link=False):

        if access:
            if access.meta.kind != 'login' or origin and origin != access.meta.origin:
                raise AccessError('Choose a login for the exact intended site.', 403)
            origin = access.meta.origin

            origin = origin or await asyncio.to_thread(self._observed_origin, turn)
            items = [item for item in self.service.delegations.items(context[0], context[1])
                     if item['kind'] == 'login' and item['origin'] == origin]
            if len(items) > 1:
                return {'status': 'account_choice_required', 'handles': [item['id'] for item in items],
                        'next': 'Ask which saved account to use.'}

        with self.service.lock_for(turn.home):

            if any(row['key'] != key for row in flows):
                raise AccessError('This task is bound to another login account. Stop its browser before switching accounts.', 409)
            row = next((item for item in flows if item['key'] == key), None)
            self.service.delegations.record_browser_use(turn, access)

                remote = self._observe(row)
                if remote.get('flow_status') == 'SUCCESS' and remote['status'] == 'AUTHENTICATED':
                    return {'status': 'authenticated', 'provider': 'kernel_managed_auth', 'handle': access.handle,
                            'next': 'Continue the original task in its authenticated Kernel browser. Inspect the website; retain all confirmed choices.'}

                    request = self._request_row(row)

                        raise AccessError('The private sign-in request expired or was cancelled.', 410)

                        (*row.values(), now, now, None, None))

                        login_url=origin, proxy_id=proxy_id, credential_name=account['credential_name'],
                        allowed_domains=[urlsplit(origin).hostname], health_checks=False, auto_reauth=False)
                    if remote['domain'] != urlsplit(origin).hostname or remote['profile_name'] != row['profile_name']:
                        raise AccessError('Kernel returned another account profile.', 403)
                    self._update(key, connection_id=remote['id'], state='starting')
                    row.update(connection_id=remote['id'], state='starting')

                    raise AccessError('Kernel sign-in creation could not be confirmed. It will not be repeated automatically.', 503) from None
        delivery = await self.service.deliver_link(request, delivery_event_id=turn.message_id if resend_link else None)

    def _start(self, row):
        try:
            request = self._request_row(row)
            if request['status'] != 'waiting' or request['expires'] <= self.store.clock():
                raise AccessError('The login request was cancelled or expired.', 410)
            login = self.client.start_login(row['connection_id'], proxy_id=row['proxy_id'])
            if login['id'] != row['connection_id']:
                raise AccessError('Kernel returned another sign-in flow.', 403)
            if not login.get('flow_expires_at'):
                raise AccessError('Kernel did not bind this sign-in attempt.', 502)
            flow = dict(state='pending', flow_expires_at=login['flow_expires_at'],
                flow_digest=hashlib.sha256(login['hosted_url'].encode()).hexdigest())
            self._update(row['key'], **flow)
            row.update(flow)
        except Exception:
            self._update(row['key'], state='login_unknown')
            raise AccessError('Kernel login dispatch is unconfirmed. It will not be repeated automatically.', 503) from None

    async def _link_delivery_receipt(self, row, member, message_ts, status):
        source = json.loads(row['source'])
        receipt = {'status': status,
                   'recipient': 'account_owner' if row.get('approver') else 'requester',
                   'location': 'private_thread' if source.get('thread_id') and not row.get('approver') else 'private_dm'}
        # An invited account's owner receives the form in their own private DM.
        # Never return that DM's permalink to the requester.
        get_link = getattr(self.policy.client(), 'chat_getPermalink', None)
        if not row.get('approver') and get_link is not None:
            try:
                result = await get_link(channel=member['dm_id'], message_ts=message_ts)
                url = result.get('permalink')
                parts = urlsplit(url) if isinstance(url, str) else None
                if (parts and parts.scheme == 'https' and parts.hostname and
                        parts.hostname.endswith('.slack.com') and not parts.username and
                        not parts.password and not parts.query and not parts.fragment):
                    receipt['message_url'] = url
            except Exception:
                pass  # Delivery is committed even if its permalink is unavailable.
        return receipt

    def _start(self, row):
        try:

    async def _link_delivery_receipt(self, row, member, message_ts, status):
        source = json.loads(row['source'])
        receipt = {'status': status,
                   'recipient': 'account_owner' if row.get('approver') else 'requester',
                   'location': 'private_thread' if source.get('thread_id') and not row.get('approver') else 'private_dm'}
        # An invited account's owner receives the form in their own private DM.
        # Never return that DM's permalink to the requester.
        get_link = getattr(self.policy.client(), 'chat_getPermalink', None)
        if not row.get('approver') and get_link is not None:
            try:
                result = await get_link(channel=member['dm_id'], message_ts=message_ts)
                url = result.get('permalink')
                parts = urlsplit(url) if isinstance(url, str) else None
                if (parts and parts.scheme == 'https' and parts.hostname and
                        parts.hostname.endswith('.slack.com') and not parts.username and
                        not parts.password and not parts.query and not parts.fragment):
                    receipt['message_url'] = url
            except Exception:
                pass  # Delivery is committed even if its permalink is unavailable.
        return receipt

    def __init__(self, directory, *, clock=time.time):
        self.directory = Path(directory)
        self.directory.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        os.chmod(self.directory, 0o700)
        self.clock = clock
        key = self.directory / 'request.key'
        if not key.exists():
            fd = os.open(key, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL, 0o600)
            with os.fdopen(fd, 'wb') as stream:
                stream.write(secrets.token_bytes(32))
                stream.flush()
                os.fsync(stream.fileno())
        self.key = key.read_bytes()
        self.path = self.directory / 'requests.sqlite'
        with self.connection() as db:
            db.executescript('''
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS requests (
                  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, team TEXT NOT NULL, owner TEXT NOT NULL,
                  home TEXT NOT NULL, task_id TEXT NOT NULL, source TEXT NOT NULL,
                  task TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL, label TEXT NOT NULL,
                  origin TEXT NOT NULL, identifier TEXT NOT NULL,
                  created REAL NOT NULL, expires REAL NOT NULL,
                  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'waiting', handle TEXT,
                  message_ts TEXT, resume_attempt REAL, resume_delivered REAL);
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS auth_states (
                  state TEXT PRIMARY KEY, browser TEXT NOT NULL, nonce TEXT NOT NULL,
                  request_id TEXT NOT NULL, expires REAL NOT NULL);
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions (
                  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, team TEXT NOT NULL, owner TEXT NOT NULL,
                  csrf TEXT NOT NULL, expires REAL NOT NULL);
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS transfers (
                  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, team TEXT NOT NULL, owner TEXT NOT NULL,
                  home TEXT NOT NULL, task_id TEXT NOT NULL, original_source TEXT NOT NULL,
                  task TEXT NOT NULL, source TEXT, created REAL NOT NULL,
                  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'waiting');
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS private_link_deliveries (
                  request_id TEXT NOT NULL, event_id TEXT NOT NULL,
                  message_ts TEXT NOT NULL,
                  PRIMARY KEY(request_id,event_id));
            ''')
            # Hermes reuses a session id across turns. Older development stores
            # made that id unique, dropping every later handoff in the thread.
            transfer_schema = db.execute("SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE name='transfers'").fetchone()[0]
            if 'UNIQUE(team,owner,task_id)' in transfer_schema.replace(' ', ''):
                db.executescript('''
                    BEGIN IMMEDIATE;
                    ALTER TABLE transfers RENAME TO transfers_legacy;
                    CREATE TABLE transfers (
                      id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, team TEXT NOT NULL, owner TEXT NOT NULL,
                      home TEXT NOT NULL, task_id TEXT NOT NULL, original_source TEXT NOT NULL,
                      task TEXT NOT NULL, source TEXT, created REAL NOT NULL,
                      status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'waiting');
                    INSERT INTO transfers SELECT * FROM transfers_legacy;
                    DROP TABLE transfers_legacy;
                    COMMIT;
                ''')
            if 'code_payload' not in {row[1] for row in db.execute('PRAGMA table_info(requests)')}:
                db.execute('ALTER TABLE requests ADD COLUMN code_payload BLOB')
            columns = {row[1] for row in db.execute('PRAGMA table_info(requests)')}
            for name, kind in [('checkout','TEXT'),('payment_payload','BLOB'),('payment_expires','REAL'),

                               ('login_method', "TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'password'")]:
                if name not in columns:db.execute(f'ALTER TABLE requests ADD COLUMN {name} {kind}')
